arguments.summary: APT-29 (Cozy Bear) activity detected originating from spearphishing attack via compromised partner email. Initial access achieved on workstation WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) through malicious attachment. Adversary executed rundll32 from temp directory, established C2 beaconing to 198.51.100.23 (later observed at 198.51.100.77), conducted credential brute-forcing via Kerberos TGT requests, and performed lateral movement using SMB to file server 10.0.5.50. Persistence established on domain controller DC-01 (10.0.8.200) via scheduled task. Detection failed to trigger on key malicious behaviors due to rule gaps and false negatives in EDR/Sandbox analysis.

timeline.description: Initial access: User CORP\jsmith opens spearphishing attachment on WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), initiating outbound HTTPS to 198.51.100.23.
Execution: Suspicious rundll32.exe process spawned from Temp directory on WS-FIN-042.
Command & Control: IDS alerts on Cobalt Strike beacon pattern to 198.51.100.23 from WS-FIN-042.
Credential Access: Multiple failed Kerberos TGT requests from WS-FIN-042 to domain controller, indicating password brute-forcing.
Lateral Movement: Successful SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to file server 10.0.5.50.
Detection: SIEM alert triggered on APT-29 TTPs with C2 beaconing to 198.51.100.77 from domain controller 10.0.8.200.

title: Suspicious rundll32 Execution from Temp Directory
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\\rundll32.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '%TEMP%'
      - '/c'
      - '-c'
  condition: selection
level: high
